identity.title: The Acr-Aca Fusion Protein AcrIF16 Dually Inhibits the Type I-F CRISPR-Cas System Through DNA Sequestration.

content.abstract: Anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins are natural inhibitors of CRISPR-Cas systems, offering valuable tools for regulating genome editing. Most characterized Acrs function through direct protein-protein interactions with Cas effectors. Here, we report that AcrIF16, an Acr-Aca fusion protein from Pectobacterium parmentieri, inhibits the type I-F CRISPR-Cas system through a DNA-binding-dependent dual mechanism without forming stable complexes with the Csy surveillance complex or the Cas2/3 nuclease. The high-resolution crystal structure of its N-terminal domain (NTD) reveals a canonical helix-turn-helix (HTH) motif that specifically binds inverted repeat sequences upstream of the acrIF16 locus. Structural prediction of the C-terminal domain (CTD) suggests a previously uncharacterized fold, although its functional role remains to be determined. Biochemical assays demonstrate that AcrIF16 binds double-stranded DNA in a sequence-non-specific manner, thereby competing with Csy for target DNA binding and destabilizing pre-assembled Csy-DNA complexes. Furthermore, AcrIF16 inhibits Cas2/3-mediated single-stranded and double-stranded DNA cleavage, an effect attributable to substrate sequestration rather than direct Cas2/3 binding. In vivo, AcrIF16 restores phage plaque formation in E. coli cells expressing the type I-F CRISPR-Cas system, supporting its anti-CRISPR activity. Thus, AcrIF16 employs a DNA-sequestration strategy to block both target recognition and DNA degradation in the type I-F CRISPR-Cas system. This work expands the mechanistic repertoire of anti-CRISPR proteins and highlights DNA-binding Acrs as a distinct class of CRISPR inhibitors.
